input.allocation: 64-byte-aligned contiguous array allocated once and reused

measurements.speedup: matching serial median wall time divided by parallel median wall time
measurements.effective_input_throughput: input bytes per run divided by median wall time, decimal GB/s; includes algorithm/runtime overhead
measurements.memory: getrusage process-wide peak RSS; platform units retained verbatim

acceptance.naive_methods: expected to lose unit terms for this cancellation pattern
acceptance.long_double_methods: must match exact reference on declared GCC/Linux CI environment
acceptance.neumaier_methods: must match exact reference for every measured run
acceptance.raw_samples: all wall and process-CPU samples retained; medians/throughput recomputed by validator

limitations: The repeated cancellation fixture is synthetic and adversarial.
A 96 MiB buffer is memory-backed but does not prove DRAM saturation; cache hierarchy, runner contention and CPU quotas may affect throughput.
Effective input throughput is not a hardware memory-controller counter and includes reduction/runtime overhead.
The fixed pattern tests one cancellation distribution only; it does not establish universal correctly-rounded behavior.
Hosted CI is not independent physical-hardware replication.
Process peak RSS is process-wide and cannot be attributed to an individual method.
Long-double precision and representation are ABI-dependent; LDBL_MANT_DIG and sizeof(long double) are recorded.
No speedup is assumed; thread startup, memory resources, scheduling and oversubscription may make parallel methods slower.
